memory_candidates.content: In this repo, context/patterns/*.md files that are @-imported directly from a skill body (not reached via context-discovery) still MUST be registered in the owning extension's index-entries.json. check-extension-docs.sh's Rule S scans every deployed context/**/*.md file and fails if it lacks an index.json entry, regardless of whether the file's real access path is direct @-import. Before assuming a new context/patterns/*.md file can skip index-entries.json registration (e.g. following a stated 'not registered' precedent), grep the precedent file itself in index-entries.json to confirm -- a stated precedent can be factually wrong.

agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/test-four-tier-conflict.sh is an intermittently flaky test under concurrent session load: it exercises task-lock.sh's four-tier conflict resolution against a /tmp scratch fixture, and occasionally fails with 'ERROR: failed to write holder.json (jq produced empty output)' due to a filesystem race, unrelated to any content change. It reliably passes when run standalone or under light system load. Treat a lone gate-8 failure on this specific test as a candidate environmental flake before assuming a regression -- verify by running the suite standalone 1-2 more times.

update-task-status.sh's target_status vocabulary is exactly research/plan/implement/pr_ready/partial/blocked -- there is no per-caller-family value like 'team-research' or 'epi_research'. When converting a caller with a domain-specific or team-specific operation name onto update-task-status.sh (via skill_preflight_update/skill_postflight_update in skill-base.sh), map it onto the nearest plain operation (team-research -> research, epi_implement -> implement, etc.) rather than trying to add a new target_status value -- the marker's own 'operation' field can safely change to match, since no consumer branches on it (confirmed empirically: skill_cleanup only rm -f's by path, skill-refresh only checks mtime).
